$comment: Documentation/projection only. Passing this schema is not PCC intake acceptance. Consumers must use the authoritative Zod record parser, per-field validation, milestone validation, and confirmation/secret-policy checks.
title: PCC Device Intake
description: One entry per permanent intake field id. Each answer records a value, its provenance, (for research/confirmed provenance) a source, and optionally a confirmation reference. x-pcc-* annotations carry the R2 policy: class, fills, requiredFor, neverDefault, confirmationRequired, sensitive, why, and evidence-primitive status.

operator.displayName.question: What name should buyers see as the operator of this device?
operator.displayName.x-pcc-why: This is the name that appears on every listing and job you accept.

operator.contactEmail.question: What email should account and job notices go to?
operator.contactEmail.x-pcc-why: We need a channel to reach you about jobs, approvals, and account security.

operator.authority.question: Is this device yours to offer, or are you setting it up for someone who decides about it?
operator.authority.x-pcc-why: Only the person who controls a device can offer it for work — this is never assumed.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Pause here and check with whoever owns or controls this device before continuing — don't guess or decide on someone else's behalf.

device.description.question: In your own words, what is this device and what should buyers expect to get from it?
device.description.x-pcc-why: This seeds device identification and the search for a matching capability contract.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Take a photo of the label and describe whatever you see — a rough guess of what it does is enough for the agent to search from.

device.vendor.question: Confirm the device's manufacturer/vendor.
device.vendor.x-pcc-why: The vendor name drives the adapter config and which kits can match this device.

device.model.question: Confirm the device's exact model.
device.model.x-pcc-why: The exact model is how we find the right manual, safety limits, and remote-control protocol.

device.serialNumber.question: What is the device's serial number (from its label)?
device.serialNumber.x-pcc-why: The serial number ties this specific unit to its device record.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Look for a printed serial number on the device's data plate or a sticker near the power input. If it truly has none, say so.

device.firmware.question: Confirm the device's firmware version.
device.firmware.x-pcc-why: Firmware version affects which commands and safety behaviors are available (N83 G8).

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Check the device's display, status page, or companion app's "About" or "System Info" screen for a firmware or software version.

device.adapterType.question: Confirm the adapter type PCC should use to talk to this device.
device.adapterType.x-pcc-why: This selects the real adapter that will run jobs — it is never "mock" for a live device.

location.cityCountry.question: What city and country is this device located in? (Shown publicly on your listing.)
location.cityCountry.x-pcc-why: Buyers need this to judge shipping time and jurisdiction — it's shown publicly, so keep it to city and country, never a street address.

location.streetAddress.question: What is the device's street address? (Private — never shown publicly; used for logistics only.)
location.streetAddress.x-pcc-why: We need this for couriers and installers, but it is never published — public listings only ever show city and country.

network.reachability.question: Is this device on the same local network as the agent host, and does it have a static IP?
network.reachability.x-pcc-why: This decides whether we can reach it directly or need pcc-node as a relay.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Ask whoever manages your network whether this device has a fixed IP, and whether it's on the same network segment as the machine running the agent.

network.outboundHttps.question: Can this device (or its host) make outbound HTTPS calls?
network.outboundHttps.x-pcc-why: Outbound-only connectivity lets us use pcc-node without opening any inbound ports.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Try loading any https:// page from a browser on the same network as the device — if that works, outbound HTTPS is very likely allowed.

network.inboundBlocked.question: Is inbound access to this device blocked by a firewall or NAT?
network.inboundBlocked.x-pcc-why: This confirms whether pcc-node's outbound-only design is required.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Ask whoever manages your router or firewall whether inbound connections to this device are blocked — most home and office routers block inbound by default.

safety.supervision.question: When it runs a job, will someone be nearby, or will it run unattended? If someone's nearby, who?
safety.supervision.x-pcc-why: Supervision level is never assumed — it directly bounds which jobs are safe to accept.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Decide whether someone will be physically present, watching remotely, or nobody at all while a job runs — this is a decision only you can make.

safety.estop.question: How do you stop this device in an emergency — for example a stop button, a power switch, or a lid switch — and where is it?
safety.estop.x-pcc-why: Before anything runs, we need a way to stop it that doesn't depend on software — this is never assumed.

safety.hazards.question: What hazards does this device present (chemical, laser, heat, mechanical, biological)?
safety.hazards.x-pcc-why: Hazard classes shape the safety envelope — an empty answer blocks job acceptance rather than assuming "none".

safety.limits.question: Here are the safety limits we found for this device, with where each came from — confirm each one, or correct it.
safety.limits.x-pcc-why: The device refuses any operation outside these limits, so they must be right for your unit — never a guess.

safety.commandRate.question: At most how many commands per minute may PCC send to this device?
safety.commandRate.x-pcc-why: The safety envelope refuses commands faster than this, so a runaway job can't overload the device.

consumables.items.question: What does each job use up — for example tips, reagents, filament, or paper?
consumables.items.x-pcc-why: This lets buyers and the scheduler know what's needed to run a job.

consumables.restockedBy.question: Who refills these consumables, and how often?
consumables.restockedBy.x-pcc-why: This sets expectations for availability and avoids mid-job surprises.

consumables.loadedMaterial.question: What material or consumable is currently loaded?
consumables.loadedMaterial.x-pcc-why: The loaded material determines which operating bands from the manual actually apply right now.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Look at what's physically loaded right now and name it as specifically as you can (brand and material, not just "filament").

calibration.lastDate.question: When did you last calibrate this device? (self-declared)
calibration.lastDate.x-pcc-why: This is self-declared only — we never infer or default a calibration date.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Check your maintenance log or the device's calibration sticker. If you're still not sure, calibrate it now and record today's date.

calibration.procedureRef.question: Which calibration procedure did you follow? (self-declared)
calibration.procedureRef.x-pcc-why: Research can suggest a procedure, but only your confirmation makes it the record — self-declared only.

evidence.executorDeviceId.question: Which device id actually executes the job?
evidence.executorDeviceId.x-pcc-why: This is the raw fact the evidence plan is built from — independence is derived from it, never asked directly.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Name the device id of the machine that actually performs the job — not a camera or sensor only watching it.

evidence.observerDeviceIds.question: Which device ids (if any) only observe the job, without executing it?
evidence.observerDeviceIds.x-pcc-why: An observer that isn't also the executor is what makes an inspection independent — we derive that, we don't ask you to assert it.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: List the device ids of any camera or sensor that watches the job without controlling it. Leave it empty if nothing else observes.

evidence.executionMode.question: Is this run against the real device, or a mock/dry-run adapter?
evidence.executionMode.x-pcc-why: A mock or dry-run answer caps the job's evidence at tier 0 — it can lower the tier, never raise it.

evidence.camera.question: Where could a camera see this job's result — does it see the work area, does it see the output, is it fixed or handheld, and which device id captures it?
evidence.camera.x-pcc-why: Buyers pay against evidence that the work happened, and what the camera can see decides how strong that evidence is.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Look for a camera already pointed at the work area or output — a webcam, a phone on a stand, a security camera. If there isn't one yet, say so; the agent can suggest a placement.

evidence.operatorPresence.question: Is an operator present always, sometimes, or never during a job?
evidence.operatorPresence.x-pcc-why: Operator presence shapes what kind of evidence and approval is realistic to collect.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Think about your usual routine: are you standing at the device while it runs, checking in occasionally, or away entirely?

evidence.approver.question: Who is the person who will approve evidence for this device? (identity only — their signing key is registered separately later.)
evidence.approver.x-pcc-why: We need to know who will attest to job quality before we register how they sign.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Name the specific person who will review job evidence for this device — a name and contact, not a role or team.

evidence.controllerRunLog.question: Can the controller export its own execution log per job? If so, via API or file?
evidence.controllerRunLog.x-pcc-why: A per-job exportable log is what lets us build a trustworthy machine execution record.

evidence.instrumentSignsOutput.question: Does the instrument cryptographically sign its own output?
evidence.instrumentSignsOutput.x-pcc-why: A self-signing instrument raises the evidence ceiling — but only once its signing key is registered (companion primitive: receipt.kernel_signed).

evidence.referenceSample.question: Do you have a reference sample with a known expected result?
evidence.referenceSample.x-pcc-why: A known-good test pair is the strongest cheap proof that the capability actually works.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Check whether you have a past output with a known-good result to compare a new job against. If not, say so — this proof method just isn't available yet.

capability.type.question: Confirm the capability contract (CSD) this device implements.
capability.type.x-pcc-why: We search the registry before authoring anything new — reuse comes first.

capability.parameters.question: Confirm the typed parameters and ranges we found for this capability.
capability.parameters.x-pcc-why: Buyers configure jobs against these typed ranges — they must be confirmed, not guessed.

pricing.unitPrice.question: What should one job cost? During the public beta, payments settle on a test network, so no real money moves yet.
pricing.unitPrice.x-pcc-why: Only you decide what your work costs — this is never assumed or guessed.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Look at what comparable services charge as a reference point, then decide your own price — a reference is never the answer itself.

pricing.minimum.question: Is there a minimum charge per job?
pricing.minimum.x-pcc-why: A minimum protects you from unprofitable small jobs — never assumed.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Decide whether a small job would be unprofitable at your per-unit price. If so, set a minimum; if not, say there isn't one.

pricing.currency.question: What currency is your price in?
pricing.currency.x-pcc-why: This is never assumed — it changes what buyers actually pay.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Decide which currency you want to be paid in — this is never assumed on your behalf.

payout.destination.question: Which wallet address should your payments go to? (During the beta this is a test-network address. Never a private key or recovery phrase.)
payout.destination.x-pcc-why: Your earnings go only where you say — this is never assumed, and the address itself is never written into this record; it goes straight to the payout store.

x-pcc-ifUnknown.check: Have your wallet address ready (a test-network address during the beta). Never type a private key or recovery phrase here.

availability.schedule.question: When can this device take jobs — for example "weekdays 9 to 5" or "any time"? Tell us the mode (always, specific windows, a cron schedule, or manual claim) and the timezone.
availability.schedule.x-pcc-why: Buyers plan around it, and jobs shouldn't arrive when nobody can refill or supervise it.

sla.acceptanceWindowSec.question: How many seconds do you have to accept an offered job before it expires?
sla.acceptanceWindowSec.x-pcc-why: This sets buyer expectations for how quickly you respond.

sla.completionDeadlineSec.question: How many seconds should a job take at most before it's considered late?
sla.completionDeadlineSec.x-pcc-why: This sets the SLA buyers see and what counts as a late job.
